passages.note: House Final Reading vote on HB2822; Weninger voted Y, but this is a general personal-property depreciation bill, not a business-attraction incentive.
Weninger was prime sponsor of HB2822, signed into law; same general depreciation-schedule bill, not an attraction incentive.

passages.provision_quote: For personal property that is initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class one, paragraph 8, 9, 10 or 13 pursuant to section 42-12001 personal property that is initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class two (P) pursuant to section 42-12002 and personal property that is acquired during or after tax year 2022 and initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class six pursuant to section 42-12006, paragraph 2 or 3, the assessor shall use a valuation factor of two and one-half percent.
passages.note: Enacted text sets a uniform depreciation valuation factor for all qualifying personal property statewide, not a conditioned or targeted incentive to attract employers.

rows.reasoning: The only evidence is HB2822 (2022), a uniform increase in the personal-property depreciation schedule applied to all qualifying business property statewide; it is a general tax-valuation rule, not an incentive 'to attract businesses' as the rungs require, and it names no wage/hiring commitments, no targeting of major employers, and no spending limits, so no rung's text is matched.
